summary: The expanded community channel rules passed 133 local Firestore emulator tests on 2026-10-18 JST: 85 community cases, including 50 new channel-management and moderation regressions, plus all 48 existing submission, judge-invitation, host and event permission cases. Metadata has strict create/update validation, administration follows the current database admin role, posting respects after-write channel state, announcements restrict posting, and moderation permits author/admin deletion without editing or cooldown resets. The overall repository score remains 1 because inherited administrator bootstrap and role-authority risks remain outside this scoped change. Production Firestore rules were deployed to hackathon-tokyo and read back as an exact match to the tested local source: ruleset projects/hackathon-tokyo/rulesets/d75ce896-b612-4a01-aa0a-53a9a9b5fcfb, updated 2026-10-17T19:15:34.118439Z (18 October JST), LF-normalized SHA-256 a3e1743fdacedebd64636cf03c49d27a17e2045f4884f82afa051f97f9d7d76f. Only the rules release changed; no production messages, channel documents or user records were created or modified for testing or deployment.

findings.check: Authority source and inherited privilege escalation
findings.issue: The existing portal-admin email bootstrap lacks an email-verification/custom-claim requirement. Existing profile, staff-assignment and invitation authority risks remain documented in submission-permissions-audit.json. The new community controls read the current stored role and do not independently repair those upstream authority paths.
findings.recommendation: Move administrator and event-role assignment to trusted server-managed authority in a separate coordinated change. Preserve the community-specific checks rather than substituting request-provided fields, display badges or the legacy email shortcut for stored administrator identity.

findings.issue: No scoped bypass found: only registered users whose current database role is admin/admins can create or edit channels, post announcements, or delete another author's message. Participants, judges, mentors, hosts and pending staff cannot manage metadata. Forged role fields, request role/admin claims, the portal-admin email shortcut and anonymous admin profiles were denied by emulator tests.
findings.recommendation: Retain the direct authority regressions and anonymous-account exclusion. Channel updated_by and message author_role are validated metadata, never the source of permission.

findings.check: Registered discovery, bounded reads and compatibility
findings.issue: No scoped bypass found: metadata and message reads require recognized registered roles. Metadata/message list queries require a limit of at most 100. Members, including pending staff and users without event membership, can discover channels and read valid closed/archived history. General, teams, judges and announcements have explicit fallback behavior without metadata; unknown or malformed configured channels cannot expose message history or accept posts.
findings.recommendation: Keep the audience explicit: these are shared community channels, not private event or staff rooms. Preserve exact application-query and fallback-channel tests when adding pagination or discovery changes.

findings.check: Channel lifecycle, announcements and immutable messages
findings.issue: No scoped bypass found: only open channels accept new messages, and announcements require a database admin. Closed/archived channels remain readable and reopen correctly. After-write validation rejects a message paired with closing an existing custom channel or a virtual default in the same atomic batch. A valid new announcement and its first admin post can be created atomically. Messages remain immutable; only their author or a registered database admin can delete them, including in archived history.
findings.recommendation: Keep lifecycle checks in both message creation and limiter validation. Preserve atomic-transition and moderator-identity tests; granting deletion must not also grant editing, re-ownership or timestamp changes.

findings.check: Metadata create/update consistency, type safety and bounds
findings.issue: No scoped bypass found: metadata create and update enforce the same exact ten-field schema, safe channel IDs up to 64 characters, bounded strings, nonblank name/section, type/status enums, integer order from 0 through 999, the authenticated updater and server update time. Invalid types, oversized values, missing/extra fields, forged updater IDs and timestamp manipulation were denied on both operations. Metadata deletion is denied even to admins; archiving preserves channel identity and history. Existing immutable message bounds and schema checks also passed.
findings.recommendation: Apply the complete validator to every future metadata write path. Do not allow parent deletion or treat malformed metadata as an open default channel.

findings.check: Atomic pairing, replay and resource abuse
findings.issue: Existing schema, ownership, server-time and three-second cross-room limiter protections passed unchanged alongside dynamic channels. Unpaired/mismatched writes, multiple messages for one limiter, limiter replay/reset/deletion and rapid posting after moderator deletion were denied. The cooldown remains per UID only; multiple accounts, repeated reads, unbounded stored history and an administrator-created catalog larger than the discovery window remain potential abuse or operational cost vectors.
findings.recommendation: Retain paired-write regressions and bounded reads. Add appropriate trusted abuse controls, monitoring, retention and catalog pagination as usage grows; do not describe a per-account delay as comprehensive spam prevention.

findings.issue: The message schema copies no account email or private profile fields, and messages are rendered as text. All registered members can nevertheless read bodies and user-chosen names, so members can voluntarily disclose sensitive information or post abusive content. Admin message removal is now supported, but reporting, moderation reasons and action-history workflows are not included in this change.
findings.recommendation: Keep the shared-audience and no-private-scores guidance visible. Consider reviewed reporting and moderation audit trails separately without exposing private user documents to resolve chat profiles.
